en: add stock a ladle at a time

does: Adds hot stock to rice a ladle at a time, stirring as each addition is taken up, so that the grains cook evenly and rub their starch off into a creamy sauce.
how: Keep the stock hot in a pot beside the pan, at a bare simmer, so that it never stops the rice from cooking.
Add enough stock to just cover the rice and stir. Keep the heat at a lively bubble.
When the pan is nearly dry and a spoon drawn across it leaves a trail, add the next ladle. Stir often and scrape the corners.
Taste along the way. Stop adding stock when the grains are tender with a small bite at the centre and the whole pan flows loosely when it is shaken.

cues.text: A spoon drawn across the pan leaves a trail that fills in slowly.
The grains are tender outside with a small firm centre, and the whole pan flows like a thick, loose cream.

mistakes.mistake: Using cold stock, which stops the cooking each time it goes in.
mistakes.fix: Keep the stock at a bare simmer beside the pan.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring in all the stock at once, so that the rice boils and the sauce stays thin.
mistakes.fix: Add it a ladle at a time and stir.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the pan dry out between ladles, so that the rice catches.
mistakes.fix: Add the next ladle as soon as the trail from the spoon stays open.

comes_after.why: The grains are coated in hot fat before any stock goes in.

variant_of.differs: A pilaf takes all its hot stock at once and is covered and left alone. A risotto takes its stock in small lots and is stirred throughout, so that the starch is rubbed off the grains into a sauce.
